solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One thing on top of another? Simple to organise in days gone by

definitions.text: One thing on top of another?

indicators.note: in places the reorganised letters within the word for bygone days

parts.note: days gone by are the past

indicators.note: to organise letters is to put them into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about stacking things, then a note that life was simpler to arrange in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to organise' rearranges SIMPLE into ALIMPSE, which goes 'in' PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript whose original writing was scraped off and written over, so one text lies on top of another.

clue.text: Soft drink without much colour

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
ale is a beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A soft drink that is nearly colourless, like lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pale has little colour, being washed-out or faint in hue.

clue.text: Priest being wicked, last character to get promotion

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is promoted, moved up to the top of this down entry

parts.note: wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A cleric behaving badly, with the final person in some ranking getting a step up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, promotion means moving up: the L at the end of EVIL goes to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was the founder of the priestly tribe of Israel, and a Levite served in the Temple, so Levi stands for a priest.

clue.text: Erudite fellow,as St Paul was

definitions.meaning: Paul wrote many of the New Testament epistles, so he was literally a man who wrote letters

explanation.surface: Describing a learned man and comparing him to the apostle Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a scholar or author, and Paul was famously a writer of epistles, the letters of the New Testament.

clue.text: Support godly person with something to get stuck into?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a godly person
a rut is a groove you can get stuck in

explanation.surface: Backing a pious person who has a task to throw themselves into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something to get stuck into' looks like an eager task, but is literally a rut in which wheels get stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a brace or bar in a framework that holds up a structure.

clue.text: Soldiers on parade will have an inclination to obey this command

definitions.text: Soldiers on parade will have an inclination to obey this command

parts.words: Soldiers on parade will have an inclination to obey this command
parts.note: the drill order makes soldiers tilt their rifles onto the shoulder, so obeying it gives an inclination

explanation.surface: A remark that troops on parade are inclined to follow a particular order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' reads as willingness, but the rifles really are set at a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Slope arms is a military drill order to carry the rifle sloped on the shoulder.

clue.text: Student events in the tabloids?

definitions.meaning: a rag is a British student fundraising event, as in rag week
a scornful word for low-quality newspapers

explanation.surface: Student events getting coverage in the popular press.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a British university charity event, often a week of stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag weeks are student charity events, and rags is slang for trashy popular newspapers.

clue.text: A superior god's trendy writing

parts.note: U stands for upper class, superior
Thor's: belonging to Thor, the Norse god of thunder
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A boast that a top deity has fashionable prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorship is the act or occupation of writing books, so it stands for writing.

clue.text: Publishing job being convenient for educationist brought in

indicators.note: brought in says the teacher's degree goes inside the word for convenient

parts.note: suiting means fitting in conveniently
BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the degree held by a teacher, an educationist

explanation.surface: A publishing post that suits someone, once an education expert has been recruited.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree, used here for the teacher holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: Subediting, preparing copy for print, is a job in newspaper and magazine publishing.

clue.text: Domestic space in no. 54, home with newly married man

parts.note: LIV is 54 in Roman numerals
in means at home
a groom is a man just married

explanation.surface: A newlywed husband settling into the house at number 54.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' after 'Domestic space' is a link word; 'home' gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A living room is the main room of a house for everyday relaxing, a space in the home.

clue.text: Attempt seen as mad on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: An effort that, thought about later, looks crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' suggests hindsight, but it means mirror-reading BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means having a try, an attempt.

clue.text: What could transform boudoire set? Me possibly

definitions.text: What could transform boudoire set? Me possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the clue as transcribed has an extra E; the setter's fodder is boudoir, a lady's private room

explanation.surface: Asking what would make over a lady's dressing room, and suggesting the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The posted clue has an extra E in 'boudoire'; the setter confirmed the clue reads 'boudoir'. 'possibly' rearranges BOUDOIR SET ME into the answer, which is furniture that could transform a boudoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom suite is a matching set of bed, wardrobe and drawers that would refurnish a boudoir, a lady's private room.

clue.text: Informally out of the groove?

parts.note: a stylus lifted from a vinyl disc is out of its groove, while the phrase also means unofficially

explanation.surface: Speaking casually about being out of one's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The groove is literally on a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something off the record means saying it unofficially, not for publication.

clue.text: Most disorganised and most aggressive?

definitions.meaning: scrappy also means keen to scrap, to fight

explanation.surface: Describing a team or person as both the messiest and the most combative.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrappy means disjointed and messy, and also, from scrap meaning a fight, quarrelsome.

clue.text: Disorderly situation in which no one pays a price?

definitions.text: Disorderly situation in which no one pays a price?

parts.words: Disorderly situation in which no one pays a price?
parts.note: a chaotic scramble, read literally as something given free to everyone

explanation.surface: A chaotic scene where nobody ends up paying.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a chaotic brawl or contest open to anyone, and read literally it means nobody is charged.

clue.text: Skilled worker, one to grumble about national organisation

indicators.note: about means the grumbler goes around the other piece

parts.note: a carper is someone who carps, grumbles
the setter meant ENT (ear, nose and throat), a hospital department; as printed this does not give those letters

explanation.surface: A tradesman who complains about some national body.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter admitted a slip: 'national organisation' should have been a hospital department, ENT (ear, nose and throat). The National Trust (NT) would leave an E unaccounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a craftsman who works in wood, a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Unusual Argentine fruit

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd fruit from Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Second chance to succeed in dire situation

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the next words

explanation.surface: Getting another go at success when things are grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the signal: the answer sits inside 'dire situation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second sitting of a failed examination, a further opportunity to pass.

clue.text: A green means stop!

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A green light meaning halt, an absurd traffic signal.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to ward it off, to stop it happening.

clue.text: Heretic spouting insane rot

indicators.note: spouting, pouring out wildly, signals the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A heretic talking crazy nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spouting' rearranges INSANE ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nestorian followed Nestorius, whose view of Christ's two natures was condemned as heresy.

clue.text: Support crazy sister about to be brought on board as businesswoman

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: brought on board means taken inside the jumbled letters
crazy signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Backing a wild sibling who joins a firm as a businesswoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' makes RIETSS; 'to be brought on board' puts the second piece inside it, as if taken aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietress is a woman who owns a business, such as a shop or hotel.

clue.text: I laid into rodent with a rope

indicators.note: laid into means placed inside the animal word

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone attacking a rodent armed with a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' sounds like an assault but here puts I inside RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a lasso, a long noosed rope used in the American West.

clue.text: Unadorned pub with minimum of excitement

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, its first letter

explanation.surface: A plain pub where little exciting happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means plain, without decoration.

clue.text: Port not drunk?

definitions.meaning: port is the ... side of a ship
a drink ... is one that remains unconsumed

explanation.surface: Port wine left unconsumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine, but is the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is the nautical term for the left side, and liquid left over has not been drunk.

clue.text: 17? No longer a maiden

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a remark about a woman who is no longer a maiden.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is RESIT; a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a test taken again, so it is an example of an exam.

clue.text: Tip a laddie constructed for waste

indicators.note: constructed means built from these letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A boy gets a tip for building something that is mere waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilapidate is an old verb for squandering or letting fall into ruin, so it means to waste.

clue.text: Ordered to land, having discharged contents

indicators.note: with its contents emptied out, only the outside letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: An aircraft instructed to come down after jettisoning its cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having discharged contents' empties LAND to LD.
explanation.definitionFit: Told can mean instructed or commanded, as in told to go.

clue.text: Lowering of standards of fellows in phony debates

indicators.note: in says the fellows go inside the jumbled letters
phony means fake, so the letters are falsely arranged

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: A complaint that sham debates by fellows mean a decline in standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phony' rearranges DEBATES to DEBASET, with MEN 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Debasement is degrading something's quality or value, a decline in standards.
